You are auditing Android/Kotlin AI-agent "skill" files for the "App architecture, MVI & modularization" topic across up to three source repos that are being merged into ONE Claude Code plugin. When multiple skills auto-trigger on the same code, contradictory guidance is a real defect.

Read the FULL content of every SKILL.md in these directories, plus any references/*.md files inside them (use Glob or Bash 'ls -R' first to discover reference files):

- [ahmed] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/everything-claude-code-mobile/skills/mvi-architecture/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)
- [ahmed] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/everything-claude-code-mobile/skills/android-patterns/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)
- [rcosteira] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/android-skills/plugins/android-skills/skills/android-dev/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)
- [rcosteira] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/android-skills/plugins/android-skills/skills/modularization/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)

Produce:
1. contradictions — cases where two sources give ACTUALLY OPPOSING advice on the SAME specific technical point (not merely different depth or wording of the same principle). Name both sources (labels: "ahmed" / "chris" / "rcosteira"), state each claim, and cite evidence (file path + the specific lines/quote).
2. bugs — code that is broken, will not compile, or is technically WRONG (e.g. catches and swallows CancellationException, loses state across config change, references undefined symbols, wrong plugin/order). severity: critical | major | minor. Cite the file + evidence.
3. depthComparison — which source is most detailed/actionable here and why.
4. uniqueValue — what each source covers that the OTHERS DO NOT (worth keeping regardless of who dominates).

Be precise; cite real file content. Do NOT invent contradictions where sources only differ in depth — that is the most common false positive. Set cluster="architecture".

2	name: mvi-architecture
3	description: Model-View-Intent architecture patterns for Android with unidirectional data flow, state management, and side effects.
4	---
5	
6	# MVI Architecture
7	
8	Unidirectional data flow architecture for Android.
9	
10	## Core Concepts
11	
12	```
13	Intent → ViewModel → State → UI
14	   ↑                        │
15	   └────────────────────────┘
16	```
17	
18	## State
19	
20	```kotlin
21	@Immutable
22	data class HomeState(
23	    val isLoading: Boolean = false,
24	    val items: List<Item> = emptyList(),
25	    val error: ErrorState? = null,
26	    val searchQuery: String = ""
27	) {
28	    sealed interface ErrorState {
29	        data class Network(val message: String) : ErrorState
30	        data object Unauthorized : ErrorState
31	    }
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## Intent
36	
37	```kotlin
38	sealed interface HomeIntent {
39	    object LoadItems : HomeIntent
40	    object Refresh : HomeIntent
41	    data class Search(val query: String) : HomeIntent
42	    data class ItemClicked(val id: String) : HomeIntent
43	    object ClearError : HomeIntent
44	}
45	```
46	
47	## Side Effects
48	
49	```kotlin
50	sealed interface HomeSideEffect {
51	    data class NavigateToDetail(val itemId: String) : HomeSideEffect
52	    data class ShowSnackbar(val message: String) : HomeSideEffect
53	    object NavigateToLogin : HomeSideEffect
54	}
55	```
56	
57	## ViewModel
58	
59	```kotlin
60	class HomeViewModel(
61	    private val getItemsUseCase: GetItemsUseCase
62	) : ViewModel() {
63	
64	    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(HomeState())
65	    val state: StateFlow<HomeState> = _state.asStateFlow()
66	
67	    private val _sideEffects = Channel<HomeSideEffect>(Channel.BUFFERED)
68	    val sideEffects: Flow<HomeSideEffect> = _sideEffects.receiveAsFlow()
69	
70	    fun onIntent(intent: HomeIntent) {
71	        when (intent) {
72	            is HomeIntent.LoadItems -> loadItems()
73	            is HomeIntent.Refresh -> loadItems(refresh = true)
74	            is HomeIntent.Search -> search(intent.query)
75	            is HomeIntent.ItemClicked -> {
76	                viewModelScope.launch {
77	                    _sideEffects.send(HomeSideEffect.NavigateToDetail(intent.id))
78	                }
79	            }
80	            is HomeIntent.ClearError -> _state.update { it.copy(error = null) }
81	        }
82	    }
83	
84	    private fun loadItems(refresh: Boolean = false) {
85	        viewModelScope.launch {
86	            if (!refresh) _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = true) }
87	            
88	            getItemsUseCase()
89	                .onSuccess { items ->
90	                    _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = false, items = items, error = null) }
91	                }
92	                .onFailure { error ->
93	                    _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = false, error = mapError(error)) }
94	                }
95	        }
96	    }
97	    
98	    private fun mapError(error: Throwable): HomeState.ErrorState {
99	        return when (error) {
100	            is UnauthorizedException -> HomeState.ErrorState.Unauthorized
101	            else -> HomeState.ErrorState.Network(error.message ?: "Unknown error")
102	        }
103	    }
104	}
105	```
106	
107	## UI Integration
108	
109	```kotlin
110	@Composable
111	fun HomeScreen(
112	    viewModel: HomeViewModel = koinViewModel(),
113	    onNavigateToDetail: (String) -> Unit,
114	    onNavigateToLogin: () -> Unit
115	) {
116	    val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
117	    val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
118	    
119	    // Handle side effects
120	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
121	        viewModel.sideEffects.collect { effect ->
122	            when (effect) {
123	                is HomeSideEffect.NavigateToDetail -> onNavigateToDetail(effect.itemId)
124	                is HomeSideEffect.ShowSnackbar -> snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(effect.message)
125	                is HomeSideEffect.NavigateToLogin -> onNavigateToLogin()
126	            }
127	        }
128	    }
129	    
130	    // Load data
131	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
132	        viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems)
133	    }
134	    
135	    HomeContent(
136	        state = state,
137	        onIntent = viewModel::onIntent,
138	        snackbarHostState = snackbarHostState
139	    )
140	}
141	
142	@Composable
143	private fun HomeContent(
144	    state: HomeState,
145	    onIntent: (HomeIntent) -> Unit,
146	    snackbarHostState: SnackbarHostState
147	) {
148	    Scaffold(
149	        snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
150	    ) { padding ->
151	        when {
152	            state.isLoading -> LoadingIndicator()
153	            state.error != null -> ErrorContent(
154	                error = state.error,
155	                onRetry = { onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) }
156	            )
157	            else -> ItemList(
158	                items = state.items,
159	                onItemClick = { onIntent(HomeIntent.ItemClicked(it)) }
160	            )
161	        }
162	    }
163	}
164	```
165	
166	## Testing
167	
168	```kotlin
169	@Test
170	fun `when LoadItems succeeds, state contains items`() = runTest {
171	    val items = listOf(Item("1", "Test"))
172	    coEvery { getItemsUseCase() } returns Result.success(items)
173	    
174	    viewModel.state.test {
175	        awaitItem() // Initial
176	        
177	        viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems)
178	        
179	        awaitItem().isLoading shouldBe true
180	        awaitItem().items shouldBe items
181	    }
182	}
183	```
184	
185	---
186	
187	**Remember**: MVI = predictable state, testable logic, debuggable flow.
188

5	
6	# Android Development Patterns
7	
8	Modern Android patterns with Kotlin, coroutines, and functional programming.
9	
10	## Kotlin Idioms
11	
12	### Immutability
13	
14	```kotlin
15	// ✅ Prefer val over var
16	val name: String = "John"
17	
18	// ✅ Immutable collections
19	val items: List<Item> = listOf(item1, item2)
20	
21	// ✅ Data class with copy
22	data class User(val id: String, val name: String)
23	val updatedUser = user.copy(name = "Jane")
24	```
25	
26	### Null Safety
27	
28	```kotlin
29	// ✅ Safe call
30	val length = name?.length
31	
32	// ✅ Elvis operator
33	val name = nullableName ?: "Unknown"
34	
35	// ✅ let for null checks
36	nullableUser?.let { user ->
37	    processUser(user)
38	}
39	
40	// ✅ Early return with null check
41	fun processUser(user: User?) {
42	    user ?: return
43	    // user is smart-cast to non-null
44	}
45	```
46	
47	### Scope Functions
48	
49	```kotlin
50	// let - Transform and return
51	val result = nullable?.let { transform(it) }
52	
53	// run - Configure and return result
54	val result = service.run {
55	    configure()
56	    execute()
57	}
58	
59	// with - Operate on object
60	with(binding) {
61	    title.text = "Title"
62	    subtitle.text = "Subtitle"
63	}
64	
65	// apply - Configure and return self
66	val user = User().apply {
67	    name = "John"
68	    email = "john@example.com"
69	}
70	
71	// also - Side effects, return self
72	val user = User().also {
73	    logger.log("Created user: ${it.id}")
74	}
75	```
76	
77	### Extensions
78	
79	```kotlin
80	// ✅ Extension functions
81	fun String.isValidEmail(): Boolean {
82	    return android.util.Patterns.EMAIL_ADDRESS.matcher(this).matches()
83	}
84	
85	// ✅ Extension properties
86	val Context.screenWidth: Int
87	    get() = resources.displayMetrics.widthPixels
88	
89	// Usage
90	if (email.isValidEmail()) { ... }
91	val width = context.screenWidth
92	```
93	
94	## Lifecycle Patterns
95	
96	### ViewModel
97	
98	```kotlin
99	class HomeViewModel(
100	    private val repository: HomeRepository,
101	    savedStateHandle: SavedStateHandle
102	) : ViewModel() {
103	
104	    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(HomeState())
105	    val state: StateFlow<HomeState> = _state.asStateFlow()
106	    
107	    init {
108	        loadData()
109	    }
110	    
111	    private fun loadData() {
112	        viewModelScope.launch {
113	            _state.update { it.copy(isLoading = true) }
114	            
115	            repository.getItems()
116	                .onSuccess { items -> _state.update { it.copy(items = items, isLoading = false) } }
117	                .onFailure { error -> _state.update { it.copy(error = error.message, isLoading = false) } }
118	        }
119	    }
120	}
121	```
122	
123	### Lifecycle-aware Collection
124	
125	```kotlin
126	@Composable
127	fun HomeScreen(viewModel: HomeViewModel = koinViewModel()) {
128	    val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
129	    
130	    HomeContent(state = state)
131	}
132	```
133	
134	## Functional Patterns
135	
136	### Result Type
137	
138	```kotlin
139	// ✅ Use Result for operations that can fail
140	suspend fun fetchUser(id: String): Result<User> = runCatching {
141	    api.getUser(id).toDomain()
142	}
143	
144	// ✅ Chain operations
145	repository.fetchUser(id)
146	    .map { it.profile }
147	    .mapCatching { decryptProfile(it) }
148	    .onSuccess { displayProfile(it) }
149	    .onFailure { showError(it) }
150	```
151	
152	### Higher-Order Functions
153	
154	```kotlin
155	// ✅ Pass functions as parameters
156	fun <T> retry(
157	    times: Int,
158	    block: suspend () -> T
159	): T {
160	    repeat(times - 1) {
161	        try { return block() }
162	        catch (e: Exception) { delay(1000) }
163	    }
164	    return block() // Last attempt
165	}
166	
167	// Usage
168	val result = retry(3) { api.fetchData() }
169	```
170	
171	### Sealed Classes
172	
173	```kotlin
174	sealed interface UiState<out T> {
175	    data object Loading : UiState<Nothing>
176	    data class Success<T>(val data: T) : UiState<T>
177	    data class Error(val message: String) : UiState<Nothing>
178	}
179	
180	// Exhaustive when
181	when (state) {
182	    is UiState.Loading -> LoadingIndicator()
183	    is UiState.Success -> Content(state.data)
184	    is UiState.Error -> ErrorMessage(state.message)
185	}
186	```
187	
188	## Resource Management
189	
190	### Context Extensions
191	
192	```kotlin
193	fun Context.dp(value: Int): Int = 
194	    (value * resources.displayMetrics.density).toInt()
195	
196	fun Context.showToast(message: String) {
197	    Toast.makeText(this, message, Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
198	}
199	```
200	
201	### String Resources
202	
203	```kotlin
204	// strings.xml
205	<string name="welcome_message">Welcome, %1$s!</string>
206	
207	// Usage
208	stringResource(R.string.welcome_message, userName)
209	```
210	
211	---
212	
213	**Remember**: Kotlin is concise. Embrace its idioms for cleaner, safer code.
214

4	  Use this skill as the baseline for ALL Android and Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) work —
5	  whenever the user mentions Android, Kotlin (in an Android context), KMP, CMP, commonMain,

11	  etc.): it routes to them and adds the few baseline rules that are easy to get wrong. Casual

15	
16	# Android / KMP baseline
17	
18	House defaults — apply them without reminders or re-derivation; where the project's actual conventions differ, follow the project:
19	
20	- **DI:** Hilt + KSP (or `android-skills:koin` when the project uses Koin). **Async:** Coroutines/Flow — no `LiveData` in new code. **JSON:** `kotlinx.serialization`. **Images:** Coil.
21	- **Network/local:** Android uses Retrofit/OkHttp + Room; KMP shared uses Ktor + Room or SQLDelight. Retrofit is Android-only — never in a shared module.
22	- **Modules:** feature-vertical packages and modules; `:core:model` has zero Android deps; `:feature:*` modules never depend on each other.
23	- **Errors:** mapped to a domain type at the repository boundary — platform exceptions never leak past it; UI state explicitly models loading / success / error (see `android-skills:android-data-layer`).
24	
25	## Skill routing
26	
27	Load the specific skill for the task, always with the **fully-qualified `android-skills:` prefix** — never the short name (`compose`, `koin`, …).
28	
29	| For | Load |
30	|---|---|
31	| Compose detail — stability, `remember`, modifiers, side effects, lists, animation, navigation | `android-skills:compose` |
32	| M3 UX — touch targets, adaptive/foldable layouts, accessibility & M3-compliance audit | `android-skills:android-ux` |

45	| Debugging — Logcat, crashes, ANRs, profiling | `android-skills:android-debugging` |
46	| AOSP / AndroidX source lookup | `android-skills:android-source-search` |
47	| Multi-module visibility & module boundaries | `android-skills:modularization` |
48	| Platform PDF annotation / page-object editing (API 36.1 / SDK ext 18) | `android-skills:pdf-annotations` |
49	
50	## New-project UI convention (greenfield)
51	
52	For a **new** project or feature with no established convention. In existing code, match what's already there — see *Reuse the project's existing mechanism* below.
53	
54	The UI layer is MVVM with an MVI-style state/effect split:
55	
56	- **One immutable `UiState` per screen**, exposed as `StateFlow<UiState>` and structured with the four buckets below. The content composable renders it and emits callbacks — nothing else.
57	- **One effects stream for fire-once imperatives** — navigate, snackbar/toast, scroll-to, share-sheet, haptics. Use `Channel(Channel.BUFFERED).receiveAsFlow()`, **not** `SharedFlow`: an effect emitted while the screen is backgrounded buffers and replays on resume instead of being dropped. Collect it in a `LaunchedEffect` (lifecycle-scoped via `repeatOnLifecycle`), never `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`. Channel-vs-`SharedFlow` rationale: `android-skills:kotlin-flows`.
58	- **State vs effect — "does it survive a config change?"** Anything still true after rotation / process death is **state** (an error to show = a field in `UiState`); anything the UI runs once and forgets is an **effect**. This is the `durable-state-over-events` rule in `compose/references/state-management.md`: keep durable things in state; the effect stream is only for one-shot imperatives.
59	- **Promote callbacks to a `@Stable Actions` interface at ~4–5+** (or when the same set is threaded through several composable layers). Below that, individual lambdas are simpler — don't abstract early. The ViewModel implements the interface; the content composable depends on `FooActions`, **never** the ViewModel, so it stays pure and previewable (a no-op `object : FooActions {}` in previews).
60	
61	```kotlin
62	data class FooUiState(/* the four buckets — see below */)
63	
64	sealed interface FooEffect {
65	    data class NavigateTo(val id: String) : FooEffect
66	    data class ShowSnackbar(val message: String) : FooEffect
67	}
68	
69	@Stable                                       // promote here once lambdas pile up (~4-5+)
70	interface FooActions {
71	    fun onItemClick(id: String)
72	    fun onRefresh()
73	}
74	
75	class FooViewModel(/* … */) : ViewModel(), FooActions {
76	    private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(FooUiState())
77	    val uiState: StateFlow<FooUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()
78	
79	    private val _effects = Channel<FooEffect>(Channel.BUFFERED)   // not SharedFlow — buffers while backgrounded
80	    val effects = _effects.receiveAsFlow()
81	
82	    override fun onItemClick(id: String) { /* _uiState.update { … } */ _effects.trySend(FooEffect.NavigateTo(id)) }
83	    override fun onRefresh() { /* … */ }
84	}
85	
86	@Composable
87	fun FooScreen(viewModel: FooViewModel = hiltViewModel(), onNavigate: (String) -> Unit) {
88	    val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
89	    val lifecycle = LocalLifecycleOwner.current.lifecycle
90	    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
91	        lifecycle.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
92	            viewModel.effects.collect { effect ->
93	                when (effect) {
94	                    is FooEffect.NavigateTo -> onNavigate(effect.id)
95	                    is FooEffect.ShowSnackbar -> { /* show snackbar */ }
96	                }
97	            }
98	        }
99	    }
100	    FooContent(uiState = uiState, actions = viewModel)   // VM passed as FooActions — FooContent sees only the interface
101	}
102	```
103	
104	> **Kotlin 2.4+:** collapse the `_uiState`/`uiState` pair with explicit backing fields (`val uiState: StateFlow<FooUiState>` + `field = MutableStateFlow(…)`) — `uiState` only, never the effects `Channel`. Full idiom + version gate: `android-skills:kotlin-flows`.
105	
106	## Four-bucket state modeling
107	
108	Screens with rich interactions (forms, calculators, multi-step wizards) get unmanageable when state is one flat `data class`. Slice `UiState` into four explicit buckets, and **derive computed values as class properties, not constructor parameters**:
109	
110	```kotlin
111	data class CheckoutUiState(
112	    // 1. Editable input — what the user types
113	    val email: String = "",
114	    val cardNumber: String = "",
115	    // 3. Persisted snapshot — last value read from the repository / stored cross-screen
116	    val savedShippingAddress: Address? = null,
117	    // 4. Transient UI-only — flags that must NOT survive the screen
118	    val isSubmitting: Boolean = false,
119	    val showCardScannerOverlay: Boolean = false,
120	) {
121	    // 2. Derived — getters, NOT constructor params, so no caller can copy() into an
122	    //    inconsistent state (e.g. emailValid = false next to a valid email).
123	    val emailValid: Boolean get() = email.isValidEmail()
124	    val canSubmit: Boolean get() = emailValid && cardNumber.passesLuhn() && !isSubmitting
125	}
126	```
127	
128	The bucket dictates lifecycle and persistence, not the field. Persisting `isSubmitting` keeps the spinner forever after process death; computing `canSubmit` outside the class lets it drift from the inputs; persisting `cardNumber` cross-screen leaks PII. Mixing the buckets produces bugs that look architectural.
129	
130	## Reuse the project's existing mechanism
131	
132	Before adding any new mechanism — an event dispatcher, an effects `Channel`/`SharedFlow`, a use-case layer, or a parallel state field — open a sibling ViewModel in the same feature and reuse what's already there. The easy miss here is **duplicating** an existing mechanism instead of widening it — adding a second `shouldDisplayUndoX` flag beside the existing one rather than generalizing the one that's there. If existing code contradicts a "best practice," follow the code and flag the inconsistency; never silently override the project's architecture.
133	
134	## Comments — earn every one
135	
136	**The test for every comment: could a reader quickly infer what it says from the code beside it? If yes, it's redundant — delete it.** A comment survives only by carrying what the code cannot: a non-obvious *why* — a decision, constraint, workaround, or gotcha. Never narrate *what* the code does; clear names and small functions already say it. "What a well-known type or call does" is a *what* the reader can look up, not a *why*.
137	
138	Write the **fewest comments that pass that test** — this holds even when a task says "make it readable" or "for juniors." Readability comes from naming and structure; a comment a newcomer needs in order to follow *what* the code does is a signal to rename or extract, not to annotate.
139	
140	**Keep** a genuine *why* (`// rethrow first — a broad catch would swallow CancellationException`), a justifying comment at a surprising call site, KDoc on a public API that adds information beyond its signature, and `TODO(owner-or-link)`. Honor an explicit request for documentation.
141	
142	**Delete on sight** — each is trivially inferable from the code beside it:
143	
144	```kotlin
145	// ---- domain model ----                                 // section-divider / banner (any width)
146	/** The user profile as the app cares about it. */        // KDoc restating the class name
147	val uiState = _uiState.asStateFlow()  // private mutable, public read-only   (restates the idiom)
148	} catch (e: IOException) {  // no connectivity, timeout, DNS failure   (restates what the type means)
149	```
150	
151	## KMP
152	
153	Inject a `CoroutineDispatcher` everywhere rather than calling `Dispatchers.Main` / `Dispatchers.IO` directly: `Dispatchers.Main` isn't guaranteed on every KMP target without the `-ktx` artifacts, and injection is also what makes dispatcher-swapped tests possible. Use `expect`/`actual` for platform specifics (file I/O, push tokens, biometrics); on iOS prefer immutable shared state.
154

2	name: modularization
3	description: Use when writing or changing any class, object, function, property, or constant in a multi-module Android/Kotlin project (settings.gradle(.kts) includes more than one module — :app, :core:*, :feature:*, :data, etc.). Symptoms — a top-level declaration left at Kotlin's default public visibility; an implementation class, mapper, helper, constant, or UI-state holder reachable from another module though only used within its own; reaching for public "because the caller needs it"; "should this be public or internal?".
4	---
5	
6	# Modularization
7	
8	**Declare everything at the lowest visibility that still compiles.** Start `private`; widen to `internal` only when another file in the *same module* needs it; widen to `public` only when a *different module* actually consumes it. Kotlin defaults to `public`, and in a multi-module project that default is usually wrong — a `public` symbol joins the module's API surface: it leaks implementation across the boundary and you are then obliged to keep it stable.
9	
10	- Public interface as the module's API → the interface is `public`; its **implementation class stays `internal`** (DI-bound, never named from another module).

contradictions.topic: How to collect the one-shot effects/side-effects Channel in Compose (lifecycle scoping)
contradictions.claimA: mvi-architecture collects the side-effects Channel in a plain, non-lifecycle-scoped LaunchedEffect(Unit) that keeps collecting even while the screen is backgrounded.
contradictions.claimB: android-dev explicitly mandates collecting the effects Channel lifecycle-scoped via repeatOnLifecycle so that effects buffer while backgrounded and replay on resume instead of firing off-screen.
contradictions.evidence: Both agree the effect stream is a Channel(Channel.BUFFERED).receiveAsFlow(), so the ONLY divergence is the collection site. ahmed mvi-architecture/SKILL.md:120-128 -> `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.sideEffects.collect { effect -> when(effect){...NavigateToDetail...} } }` (no repeatOnLifecycle). rcosteira android-dev/SKILL.md:57 -> "Collect it in a LaunchedEffect (lifecycle-scoped via repeatOnLifecycle), never collectAsStateWithLifecycle: an effect emitted while the screen is backgrounded buffers and replays on resume instead of being dropped", and the example at lines 90-99 uses `lifecycle.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { viewModel.effects.collect {...} }`. ahmed's plaint collector defeats the very buffering rationale rcosteira gives and delivers navigation/snackbar while the screen is not visible.

contradictions.topic: Where the initial data load is triggered (UI composable vs ViewModel init)
contradictions.claimA: mvi-architecture triggers the initial load from the UI: LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) } inside the composable.
contradictions.claimB: android-patterns triggers the initial load inside the ViewModel via an init { loadData() } block.
contradictions.evidence: Two ahmed skills that both auto-trigger on ViewModel/Compose code give opposing patterns for the same decision. mvi-architecture/SKILL.md:131-133 -> `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) }`. android-patterns/SKILL.md:107-109 -> `init { loadData() }`. These behave differently across configuration change: init{} runs once per ViewModel (survives rotation), whereas LaunchedEffect(Unit) re-runs when the activity/composition is recreated, re-issuing the load on every rotation.

contradictions.topic: Default dependency-injection framework for greenfield ViewModel/Compose code
contradictions.claimA: Both ahmed skills use Koin unconditionally as the default (koinViewModel()).
contradictions.claimB: House default is Hilt + KSP (hiltViewModel()), with Koin used only when the project already uses Koin.

On a new project both skills auto-trigger and emit opposing DI setup (Koin vs Hilt). rcosteira hedges by permitting Koin, so this is a divergent default rather than an absolute prohibition, but the greenfield output still conflicts.

bugs.description: The retry() higher-order function is declared as a plain (non-suspend) function but calls delay(1000) and invokes a suspend lambda block(); this does not compile.
bugs.evidence: Lines 156-165: `fun <T> retry(times: Int, block: suspend () -> T): T { repeat(times - 1) { try { return block() } catch (e: Exception) { delay(1000) } } return block() }`. Both `block()` (typed `suspend () -> T`) and `delay(1000)` (a suspend function) can only be called from a coroutine or another suspend function. The signature must be `suspend fun retry(...)`. As written the compiler rejects it: 'Suspend function delay should be called only from a coroutine or another suspend function'. It is presented under a `// ✅` heading as a recommended pattern.

bugs.description: retry() catches Exception, which swallows CancellationException and breaks structured concurrency: the loop keeps retrying (and delaying) after its coroutine scope is cancelled.
bugs.evidence: Lines 160-163: `try { return block() } catch (e: Exception) { delay(1000) }`. CancellationException is an Exception, so a cancelled block() is caught and the function retries instead of propagating cancellation. Correct form rethrows CancellationException (or catches a narrower type). Ironically rcosteira android-dev/SKILL.md:140 cites exactly this: `// rethrow first — a broad catch would swallow CancellationException`.

bugs.description: fetchUser() wraps a suspend network call in runCatching, which catches Throwable including CancellationException, so a cancelled call is converted to Result.failure and cancellation never propagates.
bugs.evidence: Lines 140-142: `suspend fun fetchUser(id: String): Result<User> = runCatching { api.getUser(id).toDomain() }`. runCatching { } catches CancellationException in a suspend context, silently defeating structured-concurrency cancellation; the recommended approach is a try/catch that rethrows CancellationException or a coroutine-aware Result helper.

bugs.description: The side-effects Channel is collected in a plain LaunchedEffect(Unit) with no repeatOnLifecycle, so effects (navigation, snackbar) are consumed while the screen is backgrounded, causing off-screen navigation and lost/mis-timed UI effects.
bugs.evidence: Lines 119-128: `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.sideEffects.collect { effect -> when (effect) { is HomeSideEffect.NavigateToDetail -> onNavigateToDetail(effect.itemId) ... } } }`. The collector stays active while STOPPED, so a NavigateToDetail emitted off-screen fires immediately on top of another destination. The buffered Channel only behaves correctly if collection pauses when backgrounded (repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)), as rcosteira android-dev/SKILL.md:90-99 shows.

bugs.description: Initial load is dispatched from LaunchedEffect(Unit) inside the composable, so it re-fires whenever the activity/composition is recreated (e.g. on configuration change), reloading data on every rotation and discarding progress.
bugs.evidence: Lines 131-133: `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.onIntent(HomeIntent.LoadItems) }`. Unlike a ViewModel init{} block (which runs once and survives config changes), LaunchedEffect(Unit) re-runs on recomposition-from-recreation, so rotation triggers a redundant LoadItems. Either move the trigger into the ViewModel or guard it with rememberSaveable.
